Madrona]] |blank1_name = Political party |blank1_info = {{Color box|{{party color|Nacionalista Party}}|border=darkgray}} [[Nacionalista Party|Nacionalista]] |blank2_name = Congressional bloc |blank2_info = Majority }} '''Romblon's at-large congressional district''' refers to the lone [[congressional district of the Philippines]] in the province of [[Romblon]]. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1919 and earlier in the [[Malolos Congress (1898)|Malolos Congress]] (National Assembly) of the [[First Philippine Republic]] from 1898 to 1901.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=21 May 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://archive.org/details/TheMalolosCongress/page/n77/mode/1up |title=The Malolos Congress: A Centennial publication on the inauguration of the Philippine Republic (January 23, 1899 - January 3, 1999) |publisher=[[National Historical Commission of the Philippines]] |date=1999 |accessdate=21 May 2020}} Romblon has been represented by a single representative elected provincewide [[at-large]] since its reestablishment as a regular province separate from [[Capiz]] in 1917.{{cite web|url=http://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l837e |title=Act No. 2724, (1917-12-07) |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=21 May 2020}} From 1943 to 1944, the district was again dissolved and reconsolidated with Capiz for the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly]] of the [[Second Philippine Republic]]. Between 1978 and 1984, regional delegations were formed in lieu of provinces for the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa|national parliament]] of the [[Fourth Philippine Republic]], with Romblon forming part of the twenty-seat [[Southern Tagalog|Region IV-A]]'s at-large district.{{cite web|url=https://www.chanrobles.com/presidentialdecrees/presidentialdecreeno1296.html#.XsZNAx4RUwA |title=Presidential Decree No. 1296 |publisher=Chan Robles Virtual Law Library |accessdate=21 May 2020}} It was restored as a [[single-member district]] in 1984. The district is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Eleandro Jesus Madrona|Eleandro Jesus F. Madrona]] of the [[Nacionalista Party]] (NP).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=21 May 2020}} ==Representation history==
